condition: Anal fissure — chronic, refractory to topical therapy
permutationLabel: Chronic (> 8 weeks), failed diltiazem; female, two vaginal deliveries
summary: 42-year-old woman with a chronic posterior fissure despite 8 weeks of topical diltiazem; two vaginal deliveries. ASCRS 2023: botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy; in women after vaginal delivery, assess continence risk (botulinum first, or anal physiology/EAUS before LIS).

inputs.hpi: Four months of pain on defaecation and bright red blood on wiping. Eight weeks of topical diltiazem 2% twice daily plus fibre with only partial relief. Two vaginal deliveries (forceps once). Continent.

exam.other: Perianal: chronic posterior midline fissure with exposed internal sphincter fibres, sentinel tag and hypertrophied papilla.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Chronic anal fissure refractory to topical diltiazem
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Chronic posterior anal fissure, refractory to 8 weeks of topical diltiazem. Botulinum toxin versus lateral internal sphincterotomy; continence risk after vaginal deliveries.

mustInclude.note: Women with previous vaginal deliveries may have occult sphincter defects; LIS carries an incontinence risk.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — management of anal fissures
guideline.section: Chronic fissure after failed topical therapy: botulinum toxin or lateral internal sphincterotomy; tailor to continence risk
guideline.citation: Davids JS, Hawkins AT, Bhama AR, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anal fissures. Dis Colon Rectum. 2023;66:190–199.

rationale: Permutation: chronicity and failed first-line treatment; continence risk. Quality only.
